glossary.Hepatocellular: Relating to the liver cells themselves.
glossary.Hepatocyte: The main functional cell of the liver.
glossary.Anorexia: Loss of appetite (not the eating disorder in this context).
glossary.Portal hypertension: Raised pressure in the portal vein carrying blood from the gut to the liver.
glossary.Encephalopathy: Brain dysfunction causing confusion, drowsiness or coma.
glossary.Chronic liver disease: Long-term liver damage lasting over six months, often leading to cirrhosis.
glossary.Fixed flexion: A joint stuck bent that cannot be straightened.
glossary.Passive movement: Movement of a joint by the examiner without the patient's effort.
glossary.LFTs: Liver function tests: ALT, AST, ALP, GGT, bilirubin and albumin.
glossary.Albumin: The main protein in blood plasma, made by the liver; low levels suggest poor liver function.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes, a blood test of kidney function and salts.
glossary.Viral screen: Blood tests for hepatitis viruses (A, B, C, E) to exclude viral causes.
glossary.Liver ultrasound: Imaging of the liver with sound waves to look at size, texture and blood flow.
glossary.Supportive care: Treatment that supports the body while it recovers, rather than curing the cause.
glossary.IV: Intravenous: given directly into a vein.
glossary.Contraindication: A reason not to give a treatment because it may cause harm.
glossary.GI bleeding: Bleeding into the gut, presenting as haematemesis or melaena.
glossary.Diuretics: Drugs that increase urine output to remove excess fluid.
glossary.Liver transplant: Surgical replacement of a failing liver with a donor liver.
glossary.End-stage: The final, irreversible stage of organ failure.
glossary.Mitochondria: The cell's energy-producing structures; damage releases mitochondrial AST.
glossary.Cofactor: A helper molecule an enzyme needs to work.
glossary.Cerebral glucose metabolism: The brain's use of glucose for energy, which needs thiamine.
glossary.Vitamin B6: Pyridoxine, a vitamin needed to make aminotransferase enzymes such as ALT.
glossary.Vitamin B1: Thiamine, needed for energy production in nerves and brain.
glossary.Synthetic function: The liver's ability to make proteins such as albumin and clotting factors.
glossary.Steroids: Corticosteroid drugs, here prednisolone, used to reduce liver inflammation.
glossary.Korsakoff syndrome: Chronic memory loss with confabulation after untreated thiamine deficiency.
